questions.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions to Exponential Equations when Rearrangement is Required
questions.problem: Given that ${e}^{-5z}-6=-2,$ find the value of $z$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{-5z}-6 & =-2 \\ {e}^{-5z} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{-5z} & =4 \\ ln⁡({e}^{-5z}) & =ln⁡(4) \\ -5z & =ln⁡(4) \\ z & =-\frac{1}{5}ln⁡(4)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z=-\frac{1}{5}ln⁡(4)$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
z≈-0.277
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Approximate Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm
questions.problem: If ${e}^{x}=6,$ then $x≈${{field-1}}, rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take $ln$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x} & =6 \\ ln⁡({e}^{x}) & =ln⁡(6) \\ x & =ln⁡(6)\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
x≈1.792
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

questions.problem: If ${e}^{5-y/2}=\sqrt[5]{7},$ then $y≈${{field-1}}, rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take $ln$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{5-y/2} & =\sqrt[5]{7} \\ ln⁡({e}^{5-y/2}) & =ln⁡(\sqrt[5]{7}) \\ 5-\frac{y}{2} & =ln⁡({7}^{1/5})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power rule to the right-hand side and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5-\frac{y}{2} & =\frac{1}{5}ln⁡(7) \\ -\frac{y}{2} & =\frac{1}{5}ln⁡(7)-5 \\ y & =-\frac{2}{5}ln⁡(7)+10\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
y≈9.222
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions to Exponential Equations when Rearrangement is Required
questions.problem: If $9-{e}^{3-4x}=5,$ then $x≈${{field-1}}, rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9-{e}^{3-4x} & =5 \\ -{e}^{3-4x} & =5-9 \\ -{e}^{3-4x} & =-4 \\ {e}^{3-4x} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{3-4x} & =4 \\ ln⁡({e}^{3-4x}) & =ln⁡(4) \\ 3-4x & =ln⁡(4) \\ -4x & =ln⁡(4)-3 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{4}ln⁡(4)+\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
x≈0.403
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
